name: Ulf Kristersson
role: Prime Minister of Sweden (since 2022) and Moderate Party leader (since 2017)
summary: Centre-right Moderate leader who governs with the Christian Democrats and Liberals, supported by the Sweden Democrats under the Tidö Agreement. His programme combines tougher criminal justice and migration policy, a work-first welfare approach, new nuclear power and NATO membership, while defending free trade, the Nordic welfare model, LGBTQ rights and abortion rights.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In 2024 he called the Nordic welfare model of general benefits and joint funding something to be proud of, said Sweden has world-class health care and that central government responsibility for care must increase.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: As opposition finance spokesman (2015-2017) he argued that the inherent ability of the market economy to let people use resources in climate-smarter ways should be trusted over left-wing steering and taxes (machine-translated Riksdag record).

tax-inheritance.rationale: On 18 April 2017 he listed the Social Democrats' earlier removal of the inheritance and gift tax among the structural reforms that produced long-term results (machine translation).

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: On 21 June 2017 he said protectionism and trade barriers are bad for everyone else and that trying to protect Swedish companies from competition would be a very bad idea (machine translation).

free-trade.rationale: He called free trade by far the best way to lift countries out of poverty (13 Nov 2019, machine translation), and as prime minister said Sweden is a strong voice for free trade and the EU should sign more free trade agreements.

social-market-economy.rationale: His 2022 government declaration says free economy and free enterprise are the basis of prosperity while the common welfare must be reliable, keeping unemployment insurance at its present level.

school-vouchers.rationale: The 2022 declaration says the Swedish free-school system is to be developed through reforms (national school-voucher norm, compulsory school choice), not abolished, while limiting early profit-taking.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The 2022 declaration keeps and develops privately run, publicly funded free schools, adding quality and ownership requirements rather than ending private provision.

work-for-welfare.rationale: His government decided in March 2026 on a bill making an activity requirement a condition for income support (prop. 2025/26:207), plus a benefit ceiling, reported in the government's own Tidö review.

rehabilitation.rationale: His government tightened parole (prop. 2025/26:34), proposed ending the prison-presumption and the multiple-offence discount and raised youth penalties, a record that shifts prisons toward punishment and protection.

decide-locally.rationale: The 2022 declaration strengthens the national role in schools and health care (inquiry into state responsibility for care, state responsibility in schools) and moves responsibility for violent youth from municipal social services to the prison service.

abortion-legal.rationale: His government decided in April 2026 on a bill allowing abortion at home and set up a constitutional inquiry on writing the right to abortion into the Instrument of Government.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In his 2024 policy statement he said it is important to preserve Sweden's rich cultural heritage.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: On 15 Sept 2021 he said everyone new in Sweden should learn Swedish and that language requirements would be introduced (machine translation); his 2024 statement stresses the individual's duty to learn Swedish.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His government cut the refugee resettlement quota to 900 a year, aligned asylum rules with the EU minimum, tightened family reunification and work-permit rules, according to the government's own review.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 2022 declaration says Sweden shall be a country where the law and gender equality apply to everyone, and the 2024 statement that everyone must live freely regardless of belief, skin colour and whom they love.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The 2022 declaration says everyone in Sweden has the right to love whom they want and the government defends LGBTQ rights against anyone who tries to curtail them.

party-controls-media.rationale: The 2022 declaration says a strong democracy requires a diversity of strong, free and independent media, and that public service funding is to be protected.

public-service-media.rationale: His government decided in 2025 on funding for public service media for 2026-2033 and issued broadcast licences, stating that their independence is to remain.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: In 2022 he said parties need not agree on everything and that boldly debating honours Swedish democracy.

collective-defense.rationale: He led Sweden into NATO (7 March 2024) and said Sweden will contribute to the security of the whole alliance and meet its obligations as a member.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He led Sweden's accession to NATO, ending 200 years of non-alignment, which he described as coming home to the free world's defence alliance.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He led Sweden into NATO, ending more than 200 years of military non-alignment, and committed Sweden to integration into NATO structures.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: On 16 May 2022 he said that for Sweden there is no reason to have nuclear weapons or permanent basing of foreign troops on its territory in peacetime and that Sweden should declare this as Finland, Norway and Denmark do (machine translation).

no-foreign-bases.rationale: On 16 May 2022 he said Sweden should, like Norway and Denmark, host no permanent foreign troop bases in peacetime (machine translation); the position is limited to peacetime.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: On 16 May 2022 he said there is no reason for Sweden to have nuclear weapons itself and relied on NATO's nuclear deterrence instead (machine translation).

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: On 16 May 2022 he said he was glad the free world, not only dictatorships, holds nuclear weapons as a deterrent never to be used (machine translation).

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He doubled defence appropriations and pledged to strengthen all branches of the armed forces and reach NATO spending levels.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The 2022 declaration expands the police (more staff and pay, density up to the EU average) and greatly expands the prison service; Civil Rights Defenders describes the agreement as widening police powers such as stop-and-search zones.

state-harmful.rationale: The 2022 declaration makes the state's core tasks (internal and external security, energy, social cohesion) the government's focus.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The 2022 declaration assigns the state duties in health care, schooling and social cohesion as well as security, saying what the state is responsible for it must do well.

total-state.rationale: The 2022 declaration says society is larger than the state and the whole of society can do more than the state alone.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The 2022 declaration treats law enforcement as a core state task and pledges an inquiry to strengthen the independence of the courts.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: His declaration and 2023 statement prioritise democracy aid to human rights defenders and democracy activists abroad.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: On 8 May 2019 he said the Moderates have said yes to Europe since 1961 because European cooperation makes the continent better, while opposing EU social-policy powers (machine translation).

expand-nuclear.rationale: His government introduced state credit guarantees and legal changes for new reactors, a nuclear roadmap, risk-sharing financing and lifted the uranium-mining ban, per the government's own review.

limit-growth.rationale: On 13 April 2016 he rejected Green policy of zero growth as running against his whole view of a good, environmentally sustainable society (machine translation).

close-ties-china.rationale: The 2022 and 2023 declarations say Sweden's China relations must rest on a common European strategy with a clear transatlantic link.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: On 8 May 2019 he said European cooperation secured peace through free trade (machine translation).

legalize-drugs.rationale: In his 28 June 2023 Almedalen speech he said narcotics are dreadful and must be fought, rejecting the myth that drugs are a Swedish exception to be tolerated.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: On 20 Sept 2016 he called a new gender equality authority silly symbolic politics, saying there are many real things to do instead (machine translation).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: On 15 Jan 2020 he said racism and anti-Semitism must never be tolerated in Sweden, and in 2024 that everyone must be able to live safely and freely regardless of skin colour.

racial-franchise.rationale: He said everyone in Sweden must live safely and freely regardless of skin colour (2024) and that racism must never be tolerated (2020, machine translation).

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He said everyone must live freely regardless of skin colour and whom they love (2024), and that racism must never be tolerated (2020).

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: He said racism must never be tolerated in Sweden (2020, machine translation) and that everyone must be able to live safely regardless of skin colour and belief (2024).

equal-outcomes.rationale: On 23 Nov 2016 he said gaps between people who work differently, and people getting rich from running their own business, are not a problem, and that rewarding effort matters (machine translation).

central-planning.rationale: The 2022 declaration names free economy and free enterprise as the basis of Swedish prosperity.

public-ownership.rationale: The 2022 declaration names free economy and free enterprise as the basis of prosperity and praises businesses as a hothouse of wealth, with no call for public ownership.

women-must-cover.rationale: His government decided in February 2026 on a criminal provision against psychological violence that includes coercion to wear religious dress such as the veil (prop. 2025/26:138).

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The 2022 declaration says Sweden shall be a country where the law applies to everyone.

one-party-rule.rationale: In 2022 he formed a government with a cooperation of four parties and said parties need not agree on everything and should debate freely, which excludes exclusive party rule.

suppress-opposition.rationale: In 2022 he said the parties should honour Swedish democracy by debating boldly, and promised a government for everyone who lives in Sweden.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 2022 declaration grounds the government's authority in the voters' mandate given to the cooperating parties at the election.

notes: Themes searched: economy and tax, trade, welfare and work, crime and punishment, migration and citizenship, energy and nuclear power, climate, NATO and nuclear weapons, EU, Ukraine, media, rights, health care, schools. His record is mostly the Tidö programme he leads, which is a four-party agreement, so only items his own government decided are counted as record, and the government's own review lists proposals and inquiries, many of which settle no statement. Same-sex marriage, gender recognition, conscription, drug policy, guns, climate attribution, unions and the death penalty were searched and found only in secondhand news or not at all, so they stay null.
